page: Amazon Web Services i4i.4xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is delivered via a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at 3.5 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs. The hardware configuration integrates 128 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector acceleration instruction sets. The server does not bundle discrete graphics hardware, provisioning zero GPUs. Local storage includes a high-capacity 3,750 GB NVMe SSD directly attached to the host, complemented by a 9 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Synthetic benchmarking demonstrates stable memory and computational throughput across multi-core tests. Geekbench results show a single-core score of 1,627 and a multi-core score of 9,799, while PassMark CPU benchmarking achieved 20,679.31 points. Memory subsystems sustained 95.9 GB/s during large-block uncached read operations and 57.32 GB/s during write operations. Database-centric operations generated a PassMark database score of 7,299.53, alongside a Redis throughput benchmark of 15.48 million SET operations per second. Compression benchmarks yielded 46.39 GB/s for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 28.19 GB/s for single-threaded gzip compression.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the provision of 3,750 GB local NVMe storage eliminates network round-trip overhead for persistent disk transactions. Tradeoffs center on the finite 16-vCPU thread ceiling and the absence of hardware accelerators, which constrains raw machine learning training tasks. Consequently, the i4i.4xlarge is technically aligned with I/O-intensive workloads, including transactional SQL engines, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time search indexing, in-memory caching tiers, and localized extract-transform-load data pipelines.

The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8375C x86_64 processor delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores at 3.5 GHz, supported by a 54 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, resulting in an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a 3,750 GB NVMe SSD, and networking operates at a 9 Gbps baseline. No discrete GPUs are included. Performance testing yields a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,799, large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 95.9 GB/s, and Redis throughput of 15.48 million SET operations per second. The server offers strong resource density for disk-intensive workloads, making it well fitted for transactional databases, NoSQL engines, distributed search indexing, and real-time analytics pipelines.
